hints: The post-collision speed of sphere $A$ is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, but its direction can either be forward ($+1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$) or rebound ($-1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$).
Use conservation of momentum $4(6) = 4v_A + 3m$ for both velocity cases to determine the two possible values of $m$.
Calculate the loss in kinetic energy: $\Delta E_k = E_{k, \text{initial}} - E_{k, \text{final}}$ for each value of $m$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the system ($u_A = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $u_B = 0$):
$$E_{k, \text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(6^2) = 2 \times 36 = 72\text{ J}$$

Case 1: Sphere $A$ continues in its original direction with $v_A = +1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_B = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$4(6) = 4(1.5) + 3m$$
$$24 = 6 + 3m \implies 3m = 18 \implies m = 6\text{ kg}$$
Calculate final kinetic energy and loss:
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(1.5^2) + \frac{1}{2}(6)(3^2) = 4.5 + 27 = 31.5\text{ J}$$
$$\text{Loss} = 72 - 31.5 = 40.5\text{ J}$$

Case 2: Sphere $A$ rebounds with velocity $v_A = -1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_B = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$4(6) = 4(-1.5) + 3m$$
$$24 = -6 + 3m \implies 3m = 30 \implies m = 10\text{ kg}$$
Calculate final kinetic energy and loss:
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(1.5^2) + \frac{1}{2}(10)(3^2) = 4.5 + 45 = 49.5\text{ J}$$
$$\text{Loss} = 72 - 49.5 = 22.5\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Calculating Mechanical-Energy Changes: Considers both directions for $A$ to get $m = 6\text{ kg}$ and $m = 10\text{ kg}$, then computes KE losses of $40.5\text{ J}$ and $22.5\text{ J}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum for the direct collision:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
Given $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$, $u_A = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $u_B = 0$, and $v_B = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$4 \times 6 + 0 = 4 v_A + m(3)$$
$$24 = 4 v_A + 3m$$
The speed of $A$ after collision is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which admits two physical directions:

Case 1 ($A$ continues in the positive direction, $v_A = +1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$24 = 4(1.5) + 3m$$
$$24 = 6 + 3m$$
$$3m = 18 \implies m = 6\text{ kg}$$
Compute initial and final kinetic energies:
$$E_{k, \text{before}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(6^2) = 72\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k, \text{after}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(1.5^2) + \frac{1}{2}(6)(3^2) = 4.5 + 27 = 31.5\text{ J}$$
Subtract to find the loss in kinetic energy:
$$\text{Loss} = 72 - 31.5 = 40.5\text{ J}$$

Case 2 ($A$ rebounds in the negative direction, $v_A = -1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$24 = 4(-1.5) + 3m$$
$$24 = -6 + 3m$$
$$3m = 30 \implies m = 10\text{ kg}$$
Compute initial and final kinetic energies:
$$E_{k, \text{before}} = 72\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k, \text{after}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(1.5^2) + \frac{1}{2}(10)(3^2) = 4.5 + 45 = 49.5\text{ J}$$
Subtract to find the loss in kinetic energy:
$$\text{Loss} = 72 - 49.5 = 22.5\text{ J}$$
